root_cause.text: The b43_rx() function uses a firmware-supplied key index without a runtime bounds check, relying only on a non-enforcing B43_WARN_ON, allowing an out-of-bounds read when the firmware provides an index exceeding the dev->key[] array size (58 entries).
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "The firmware-controlled key index in b43_rx() can exceed the dev->key[] array size (58 entries). The existing B43_WARN_ON is non-enforcing in production builds, allowing an out-of-bounds read." The fix changes the non-enforcing `B43_WARN_ON(keyidx >= ARRAY_SIZE(dev->key));` to an enforcing check: `if (B43_WARN_ON(keyidx >= ARRAY_SIZE(dev->key))) goto drop;`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to drop the received frame if the key index is out of bounds, preventing out-of-bounds array access.
intent_record.what: Replaced a standalone B43_WARN_ON macro with an if statement that calls B43_WARN_ON as the condition and jumps to 'drop' label when the condition is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if keyidx is out of bounds, a warning is printed and the code jumps to the 'drop' label, dropping the received frame instead of continuing and potentially accessing out-of-bounds memory.
